findings.passage: The intent of this bill is to create consistency within existing Kentucky law, while more importantly recognizing the right to keep and bear arms. It allows Kentuckians aged 18 to carry a concealed firearm. The governor vetoed HB 312 on the grounds of age comparisons and other unrelated restrictions. However, under current law, 18-year-olds can already openly carry a firearm. This bill simply allows them to obtain a concealed carry license through a legal process that includes training and accountability, which I argue the governor should appreciate.
findings.note: Williams, in a legislative-update column under his name on a county party site, explains HB 312 (concealed carry licence for 18-year-olds) after the governor's veto and says it recognises the right to keep and bear arms.
subjects: carry a concealed gun at age 18
right to keep and bear arms

findings.passage: This bill addresses liability standards for manufacturers and sellers. The governor framed it as limiting legal recourse, but the legislation aligns with long-standing principles that producers are not responsible for the criminal misuse of lawful products. These standards that the governor would apply to gun manufacturers do not apply to manufacturers of other products, nor are such products outlined as an inalienable right in the Bill of Rights.
findings.note: In the same column, Williams describes HB 78 (liability standards for gun makers and sellers) after the governor's veto, saying makers should not be held responsible for criminal misuse of lawful products.
